nodes.title: Start each attempt inside a resolved promise
nodes.why: A synchronous throw inside fn becomes a rejection of the chain, so one catch handles both failure kinds.
nodes.alternative: Call fn() directly inside a try/catch and also attach a catch to the returned promise.
nodes.tradeoff: One extra microtask per attempt, but a single failure path.

nodes.title: Resolve the outer promise on the first success
nodes.why: A promise settles once, so resolving here ends the retry loop; no later attempt can change the result.
nodes.alternative: Keep a settled flag and check it before every step.
nodes.tradeoff: Relies on settle-once semantics instead of extra state.

nodes.title: Count attempts left, not attempts made
nodes.why: The exit test is one comparison and retries naturally means extra attempts after the first.
nodes.alternative: Count attempts made and compare with retries + 1.
nodes.tradeoff: Either works; counting down reads as retries left.

nodes.title: Schedule the next attempt after the delay
nodes.why: The pause belongs between attempts only; the first attempt starts immediately and the final failure rejects without waiting.
nodes.alternative: Await a sleep helper inside an async loop.
nodes.tradeoff: Callback nesting instead of async/await, but no helper needed.

nodes.title: Loop retries + 1 times
nodes.why: An inclusive upper bound makes the attempt count explicit: one first attempt plus retries extra ones.
nodes.alternative: Loop while a counter is greater than zero and decrement it.
nodes.tradeoff: Inclusive bounds are easy to misread; the comment in the contract keeps it honest.

nodes.title: Await inside the try block
nodes.why: Awaiting inside try means both rejections and synchronous throws land in the catch below.
nodes.alternative: return fn() without await and attach catch handlers.
nodes.tradeoff: return await costs one microtask but keeps the control flow linear.

nodes.title: Sleep only when another attempt follows
nodes.why: The last failure should reject immediately instead of sleeping first.
nodes.tradeoff: One comparison saves a pointless delay at the end.

nodes.title: Throw the last error after the loop
nodes.why: The caller needs the most recent failure, not the first one.
nodes.alternative: Collect every error into an AggregateError.
nodes.tradeoff: A single error matches most callers; AggregateError is a reasonable follow-up.
